svg.aria-label: A continuous ink drawing for the Netherlands: the teacher's advice is drawn first as a short horizontal dash at mid-height on the left — a track assigned. From the right a second dash arrives firmer at a higher level: the test's reading. Between them, the only warm mark on the page, a small kiln-orange arrow curves upward from the lower dash to the higher — the mandatory upward revision, the lever fixed by law. But the arrow is drawn twice more, fainter, further into the page: once complete, once half-risen, once barely begun — the lever pulled fully in one town and hardly at all in another; the height reached rides on where the child stands.
svg.title: The Still · Netherlands — the lever fixed by law, pulled fully in one town and hardly in another
svg.desc: Paper-cream ground, pure line, no fills. A lower reference line carries the teacher's advice; a higher reference line carries the test's reading. Three kiln-orange arrows rise from the lower line toward the higher across the page — the mandatory upward revision. The first reaches the top fully; the second climbs only halfway; the third barely leaves the lower line — the same legal lever, gripping unevenly by town and class.
